sections.theory:
Chapter Six: Arabic language and literature

Teaching objectives

The purpose of this lesson is to enable the students that they: acquire so much skill in the Arabic language that they can read and understand Islamic teachings in the Arabic text.

Study of the Arabic language

Before the sun of Islam rose, Arabic literature was at its peak. Especially in poetry the Arabs had attained perfection, and every tribe used to take pride in its poets. And if some tribe had no poet, it was considered a cause of shame for it. The Arabs considered themselves more eloquent than all other people. One meaning of 'Arab is also one possessing a clear and lucid tongue, and in contrast to it they used to call non-Arabs 'Ajam, whose meaning is dumb. In these circumstances Allah the Exalted sent His last Messenger ﷺ and sent down the Holy Quran upon him, which made the tongues of the Arabs, who used to call themselves very eloquent, dumb. They began to say, "Is it the poetry of some poet, or the sorcery of some sorcerer, or the rhymed speech of some soothsayer?" (Tarikh al-Adab al-'Arabi, Ahmad Hasan al-Zayyat, p.67, al-Maktabah al-'Ilmiyyah)

Chapter Six: Arabic language and literature

Teaching objectives

The purpose of this lesson is to enable the students that they: acquire so much skill in the Arabic language that they can read and understand Islamic teachings in the Arabic text.

Study of the Arabic language

Before the sun of Islam rose, Arabic literature was at its peak. Especially in poetry the Arabs had attained perfection, and every tribe used to take pride in its poets. And if some tribe had no poet, it was considered a cause of shame for it. The Arabs considered themselves more eloquent than all other people. In these circumstances Allah the Exalted sent His last Messenger ﷺ and sent down the Holy Quran upon him, which made the tongues of the Arabs, who used to call themselves very eloquent, dumb. They began to say, "Is it the poetry of some poet, or the sorcery of some sorcerer, or the rhymed speech of some soothsayer?"
